title: Search a 2D Matrix II
statement: Every row increases left to right and every column increases top to bottom, but unlike Search a 2D Matrix the rows do NOT continue from one another: the first value of a row may be smaller than the last value of the row above. Return whether the target is present.
constraints: rows are sorted ascending and columns are sorted ascending
flattening to one sorted list is not valid here
hints: Binary searching each row is O(rows log cols) and ignores the column ordering. There is a linear walk that uses both orderings at once.
Look for a corner where the two directions disagree - one where going one way always increases and the other always decreases. The top-right is such a corner.

Stand at the top-right. If the value is larger than the target the whole column is too large, so move left; if smaller, the whole row is too small, so move down. Each step retires a row or a column, giving O(rows + cols). The bottom-left corner works identically.
